scenes.line1: How does Angular link logic and UI?
scenes.say: How does Angular connect your code to what users see? Let's break down components and data binding.

scenes.label: Component
scenes.sub: TypeScript class, template, and CSS shape the UI.
scenes.say: A component in Angular is made of a TypeScript class, an HTML template, and optional CSS. It's the core building block of your UI.
Data binding links your component's logic to the template. Use property binding to push data to the view, event binding to react to user actions, and two-way binding to keep both in sync.
Here's an example: property binding with user in square brackets, and event binding with save in parentheses. This keeps data and UI in sync.

scenes.question: What do square brackets mean in templates?
scenes.right: Square brackets set properties or inputs from your component to the view.
scenes.say: Careful—square brackets in templates mean property binding, not event handling. Interviewers love to test this distinction.
